newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINA APPALLED AT BOLIVIA RIOT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA APPALLED AT BOLIVIA RIOT.

text.p: Argentina's press reacted with horror and indignation on Thursday to a soccer clash in Bolivia which left their team both physically bruised and in danger of missing the 1998 World Cup finals in France.

Sports writers shook their heads in response to a match pockmarked with incidents and interrupted for 10 minutes by a brawl involving players and police. On top of that, Argentina performed badly again and lost 2-1.

"Argentina played poorly and the police played dirty," was the front page headline in Clarin, the biggest selling paper in the Spanish speaking world. Clarin put most of the blame for the incidents on the Bolivians, especially the police.

"The cowardly attack on the physiotherapist Hernan Arsenian, the treacherous punch thrown at Julio Cruz, the paralyzing gas that knocked out Roja," Clarin wrote. "But these attacks, which perhaps put the Hernando Siles stadium among those considered dangerous, cannot wipe out the shame caused by the unintelligent attitude of the Argentine players."

La Nacion wrote that the Argentina team turned to violence when they realized they were losing despite three weeks of altitude training in the Andes to prepare for the match in La Paz, at 14,000 feet (3,600 metres) above sea level.
"The Argentines started the fight, but the Bolivians accepted the ridiculous invitation and stepped up to a higher level of violence," La Nacion said.
Diego Maradona blamed the Bolivians for the scenes, accusing them of cowardice.
"You ever hear of a famous Bolivia boxer? They're a bunch of cowards man," he told local radio.
Two Argentines were sent off during the match before the first all-out fight, which broke out after Argentina's Gustavo Zapata refused the referee's order to leave the pitch.
In the chaos, Argentine goalkeeper Ignacio Gonzalez escaped unpunished after viciously headbutting Bolivian substitute Demetrio Angola from behind and knocking him to the ground.
But the biggest brawl began near the end when Cruz ran off the pitch to fetch the ball near the Bolivian bench.

Bolivian team assistant Javier Avila punched Cruz several times and knocked him down. Other Argentine players and Bolivian riot police joined in the fight whilst spectators hurled projectiles at everybody. A policeman left Argentina's Carlos Roja in severe pain by spraying him in the face with gas.
"They beat us at soccer and at boxing too," lamented one fan in Buenos Aires.

Argentina's much-criticized coach Daniel Passarella said he would complain to the South American Football Confederation. Clarin speculated that Argentina might argue it should get the three points for victory instead of Bolivia.
But two-time world champions Argentina, trailing fifth in the South American qualifying group, need to improve if they are to make it to France.
